title: Backend: content-actions Lambda exposing derive/save/publish/unpublish to the newsroom app
description:
## Goal
Expose derive/save/publish/unpublish to the newsroom app through AppSync, so the browser never has to run Python and `bodyIr` is always produced by the same code the CLI uses. One new Python Lambda `papyrus-content-actions` with four GraphQL operations, authorized for the `editor` and `admin` Cognito groups.

## Context (verified)
- Python Lambda pattern to copy: `amplify/functions/knowledge-query/` (`resource.ts` uses `defineFunction((scope) => new Function(...))` with `Runtime.PYTHON_3_12`, `Architecture.ARM_64`, `handler: "handler.handler"`, `pythonLambdaCode({functionDir, modules, requirements?, checkoutExtras?}, dockerCommand)` from `amplify/functions/shared/python-bundle.ts`, `{ resourceGroupName: "data" }`). Checkout mode copies `src/<module>` and does NOT install dependencies unless `checkoutExtras` does (see `amplify/functions/email-submission-processor/resource.ts`: `requirements.txt` + `installPythonRequirements`). Package mode (`@anthusai/papyrus` installed in a publication repo) does `pip install papyrus-newsroom==<this version> --platform manylinux2014_aarch64 --only-binary` plus `options.requirements`.
- GraphQL wiring pattern: `amplify/data/schema.ts` L405-412 `knowledgeQuery: a.query().arguments({ input: a.json().required() }).returns(a.json()).authorization((allow) => [allow.groups(categoryWriteGroups), allow.custom()]).handler(a.handler.function(knowledgeQuery))`; schema-level `.authorization((allow) => [allow.resource(categoryAction), ...])` near L1938 (grants the Lambda IAM access to the models). The same list exists in `amplify/data/resource.ts` L2113-2121 (duplicate schema; keep in sync, see `PPY-44a0f9`). Lambda registered in `amplify/site-backend.ts` (`defineBackend({... knowledgeQuery ...})` L92-95; `grantNewsroomReadWrite(...)` L357-402).
- In Lambda the authoring client uses IAM (`graphql_http.graphql_use_iam()`, `running_in_aws_lambda()`), endpoint from `APPSYNC_ENDPOINT`-style env; read `graphql_http.py` and `env.graphql_endpoint()` for the exact variable and how `knowledge-query` gets it.
- Model logic is `PPY-b3a10e` (`papyrus_content.publishing.save_item/publish_item/unpublish_item`) and `PPY-e169c5` (`derive_body`).

## Exact changes
1. `amplify/functions/content-actions/resource.ts` (new): `export const contentActions = defineFunction(...)`, python3.12/arm64, timeout 60 s, memory 1024 MB, modules `["papyrus_content"]`, `requirements` (checkout mode via `checkoutExtras` + `requirements.txt`): `PyYAML>=6.0.2,<7`, `citeproc-py>=0.8.2,<1`, `anthus-markus==0.5.1`, `Pillow>=10,<12`. Package mode: add `noDeps?: boolean` to `PythonBundleOptions` in `python-bundle.ts` (adds `--no-deps` to the `papyrus-newsroom` pip spec only, then installs `requirements`) and use it here, because the wheel's base deps include `limatus` (heavy) that this function never imports. Assert in a unit test that the built asset directory is < 100 MB.
2. `amplify/functions/content-actions/handler.py` (new):
   ```python
   def handler(event, context):
       field = event["info"]["fieldName"]       # deriveMarkus | saveItemDraft | publishItem | unpublishItem
       args = event["arguments"]["input"]       # AWSJSON string or dict
       actor = (event.get("identity") or {}).get("username") or (event.get("identity") or {}).get("sub") or "unknown"
   ```
   Parses `input` (`json.loads` if str), calls `derive_body` / `save_item` / `publish_item` / `unpublish_item` with a `PapyrusGraphQLAuthoringClient` built by `create_authoring_client()` (IAM in Lambda). Returns a JSON-serializable dict; catches `PublishError` and returns `{"ok": false, "errors": [...]}` (never raise for validation problems; raise only for unexpected failures so CloudWatch shows a stack).
3. `amplify/data/schema.ts` AND `amplify/data/resource.ts`: add four operations next to `knowledgeQuery`:
   ```ts
   deriveMarkus:   a.query().arguments({ input: a.json().required() }).returns(a.json()).authorization((allow) => [allow.groups(contentWriteGroups)]).handler(a.handler.function(contentActions)),
   saveItemDraft:  a.mutation().arguments({ input: a.json().required() }).returns(a.json()).authorization(...same...).handler(...),
   publishItem:    a.mutation()...,
   unpublishItem:  a.mutation()...,
   ```
   plus `allow.resource(contentActions)` in the schema-level authorization list and `import { contentActions } from "../functions/content-actions/resource";`. No `allow.custom()` here (staff only through Cognito groups; the JWT lane is for CLIs that call the Python module directly).
4. `amplify/site-backend.ts`: import `contentActions`, add it to `defineBackend({...})`, `grantNewsroomReadWriteDelete(backend.contentActions.resources.lambda as LambdaFunction)` (publish deletes rows), pass the AppSync endpoint env the same way other Python Lambdas get it.
5. `lib/content-actions-client.ts` (new, TS, used by `PPY-8ef4ca`): typed wrappers `deriveMarkus(input)`, `saveItemDraft(input)`, `publishItem(id)`, `unpublishItem(id)` calling `generateClient<Schema>().queries.deriveMarkus({ input: JSON.stringify(...) }, { authMode: "userPool" })` / `.mutations.*`; parses the returned JSON; export the TS types below.

## Data shapes
Requests (the `input` JSON):
```text
deriveMarkus:   {"frontMatterYaml": "title: T[LF]", "bodyMarkus": "Hello **x**"}
saveItemDraft:  {"id": null, "type": "article", "slug": "my-post", "section": "articles", "frontMatterYaml": "title: T[LF]", "bodyMarkus": "...", "aliases": [], "expectedContentHash": null}
publishItem:    {"id": "item-abc"}
unpublishItem:  {"id": "item-abc"}
```
Responses:
```text
{"ok": true,  "bodyIrBytes": 1234, "errors": []}                                   // deriveMarkus (+ "bodyIr" only when the request has "includeIr": true)
{"ok": true,  "item": {"id": "...", "contentHash": "sha256:...", "status": "draft", "slug": "...", "versionNumber": 1}}   // saveItemDraft
{"ok": false, "errors": [{"code": "markus-syntax", "message": "...", "line": 12}]}   // validation failure
{"ok": true,  "changed": true, "publishedId": "published-item-abc", "versionNumber": 2}   // publishItem
{"ok": true,  "changed": true}                                                      // unpublishItem
```
Error codes: those of `BodyError` (`PPY-e169c5`) plus `conflict`, `slug-locked`, `not-found`.

## Tests
- Unit: `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_content_actions_handler.py`: call `handler()` directly with fabricated AppSync events and a monkeypatched client factory returning `FakeAuthoringClient` (from `PPY-b3a10e`): derive ok/bad, save new then save with stale hash -> `conflict`, publish then `PublishedItem` exists, unpublish removes it; unexpected exception propagates.
- TS: `scripts/test-content-actions-client.ts` (tsx): the wrapper serializes `input` and maps `{ok:false}` to a typed error (mock the client).
- Gherkin: `features_backend/content-actions.feature` + steps: "An editor derives, saves, publishes and unpublishes an article through the content actions".
- Sandbox (AWS; `AGENTS.local.md`): `npx ampx sandbox`; with an editor JWT call `deriveMarkus` via the AppSync console or a tiny script; the PR records the response. Non-editor Cognito user gets `Unauthorized` (spike PPY-82be6c script `scripts/spike-auth-test.mjs` pattern: create test users in the script, delete them in a `finally`, random in-memory password, print nothing secret).

## Acceptance checks
- `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.test_content_actions_handler -v`, `poetry run behave features_backend/content-actions.feature`, `npx tsx scripts/test-content-actions-client.ts`, `npx tsc --noEmit` all pass.
- `npx ampx sandbox` deploys; `poetry run papyrus content schema-check --type Query --fields deriveMarkus` and `... --type Mutation --fields saveItemDraft,publishItem,unpublishItem` print `schema-check\tok\ttrue`, and a signed-in `editor` gets `{"ok": true}` from `deriveMarkus`.
- Asset size check passes (< 100 MB unzipped).

## Dependencies
Blocked by `PPY-44a0f9`, `PPY-e169c5`, `PPY-b3a10e`. Blocks `PPY-8ef4ca` (UI calls these), `PPY-fbb1fb` (adds the rebuild call inside `publishItem`). Same-file conflicts: `amplify/data/schema.ts`, `amplify/data/resource.ts`, `amplify/site-backend.ts` (also `PPY-44a0f9`, `PPY-fbb1fb`, `PPY-39f928` for config types).

## Risks
- Bundle size and cold start in package mode (`limatus`): mitigated by `noDeps`; measure.
- AppSync resolver timeout is 30 s; a publish with many media rows is a handful of calls, fine; if a content-heavy publish ever exceeds it, the CLI path remains.
- The schema-level `allow.resource(contentActions)` grants the Lambda read/write on ALL models (same as the existing action Lambdas); this is the repo's current pattern, not a new exposure.
- Keep `deriveMarkus` cheap: it is called while typing (debounced, `PPY-8ef4ca`), so it must not call AWS; it only parses.

## Needs Ryan
Nothing.

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-3e5235-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).

- Notation: `[LF]` in this ticket text means a newline character (the board tool cannot store a backslash followed by n).
right_now_summary: A new Lambda will expose content derivation, saving, publishing, and unpublishing through AppSync.
